item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Okay, here goes:

+ show block
– hide block

Immediately from the containment, the information is rather jumbled. Try to structure the containment from establishing the most immediately pertinent visualization aspects first (in this case, the fact that the anomaly is in a provisional site) and then moving from subject to subject for each aspect of requirements (staffing, maintenance, access, etc.). Also, try to trim down the length of the sentences that are simple "don't do this" commands. For example:

It is only to be entered by Level 2 cleared staff and only for research or cleaning purposes.

No water originating from SCP-XXXX is to be used for cleaning and no liquids from outside of SCP-XXX are to be inserted into the facilities.

At no time should SCP-XXXX be used as sanitary facility.

You could just make a quick bullet list with parallel structure so the directions aren't as roundabout. For example:

Personnel accessing SCP-XXXX may not:

  • Enter the anomaly if not performing research or cleaning.
  • Use water produced by SCP-XXXX for cleaning.
  • Insert liquids from outside SCP-XXXX into the facility.
  • Use SCP-XXXX as a sanitary facility.

Remember that clinical tone does not mean using a lot of words to describe something simple. In that same vein, you don't need to use phrases like "at no time" and "at all times" since it's assumed that unless otherwise stated, containment procedures are always in place.

There are also a lot of small errors, such as:

  • Typically authorization levels have hyphens. So Level-2 and not Level 2.
  • Vague instructions. "Cleaning staff are to flush if they hear noises coming from SCP-XXXX" > what exactly are they flushing? What sort of noises?
  • and must make record of doing so. > there should be a standardized log system rather than just "record it somewhere". Ideally, there would be some sort of cleaning report that could be referenced for this sort of thing. "Make record" could be anything from a cell phone call to a post-it note to a formal write-up.
  • I'm not certain if "port-a-potty" would be considered clinical phrasing. "Portable toilet" or "alternative restroom facilities" would be taken more seriously.
  • SCP-XXXX is to be locked at all times unless Level 2 staff requires to enter the SCP. > this should be placed earlier in the instructions. Also, Level-2 staff is a very wide body of individuals; it would make more sense to just note "personnel assigned to SCP-XXXX" or the like. Also, don't refer to an anomaly as "the SCP" (SCP refers to the containment procedures or the Foundation motto). In-universe, the non-slang way to reference this anomaly would just be "SCP-XXXX" or "the restrooms".
  • and so on.

The description is similarly full of small errors in clinical tone and Foundation presentation; the most notable issue is that the anomalous effects are not made immediately clear. There's no need to have the background investigation noted before the effects of drinking the tap water. This is another case where a bullet-point list could be of use, to introduce all of the small anomalous effects together so the reader isn't left wondering why the Foundation bothered containing the location.

The Audio Transcript portion just feels a little sloppily written because the dialogue feels wooden (Frank in particular sounds more like a robot trying to imitate human speech than an actual human talking in the moment) and there are again small errors ("lets" is missing an apostrophe). As a reader, I'm unsure of what the log is meant to convey besides typical "something unknown but bad happened because the place is spooky and something happened to the robot" tension. It feels a little forced and as a result I feel skeptical more than scared.

The Incident Report just feels almost tacked on as an afterthought. I'm not sure why "Michael" needed to be italicized, and the suddenness of the anomaly hurting someone and behaving oddly comes kind of out of nowhere. It would have been better pacing if that sort of effect had been introduced or at least more clearly hinted at in the description. And then at the end of the incident report I as a reader am still unsure about what's going on and why I should care about the anomaly. It messes with people's digestive systems apparently… for what reason? If you don't intend to have an in-universe reason for the manifestation, there needs to at least be a more meaningful takeaway at the end of the article (could have been something like "is the Foundation justified in starving the thing?" or "should the Foundation try to introduce appetite suppressants?") beyond just "okay it can actually do scary things, update the containment".

Overall I feel like the article needs a fair bit of general restructuring so the basic anomaly information and plot flow better. The storyline in particular needs to move more fluidly from the description to the addenda; right now each part feels almost like separate portions of the story with the in-between material removed. As such, it feels jumpy and sudden and disconnected, rather than a followable investigative process of understanding the anomaly.

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Followup response to PM:

I personally didn't find the draft that interesting—it seemed like the majority of the description was about the non-anomalous features. The actual anomaly itself wasn't clear until I reread the entirety of the description. The logs were pretty bland and generic horror material, especially the last log that had an incident that seemed gratuitous/shoehorned just to artificially introduce previously unmentioned danger.

Would you like a full review of the draft (there were a lot of small clinical tone errors, and spots where I felt the text could be slimmed down) or would you like me to discuss the concept first?

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
I gave your draft a read through. Please note, I'm not a critter and will be providing feedback as a reader / author.

Crit
Hide

Your formatting of the ConProcs is visually distracting. The hallway is located within Provisional Site-XXXX, so you should establish the existence of the site first instead of at the end. The post-incident adjustments can be incorporated into the normal ConProcs; having it as an add-on doesn't benefit the story or anything.

Your description should state what the SCP is first, then where it is located. The description still has general grammar errors and a lot of text that comes off as non-clinical.

I lost interest after the description because there just really isn't anything interesting there. In a 340 word description, all you've really told me is that it's two washrooms (one for men, one for women) not connected to utilities but still working inside an office building.

If the "meat" comes later, it's important to ensure the reader doesn't become uninterested before then.

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded: Thanks for the crit. I hope I fixed it, reworked the spacing in the article and shifting the containment. I have a "post-incident" section in the containment, don't know if that is ok or not. Unfortunately I don't really know what you mean with inconsistent section heading capitalization, looks fine to me (or do you mean the lowercase "report"?)

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this.

I took a quick look at the draft. There are a lot of simple errors, such as lack of correct paragraph spacing, unnecessary crossed-out materials in the containment (try to avoid redacting or withdrawing anything in that section; if you really must include earlier versions of containment, I recommend having an archived version in a collapsible), and inconsistent section heading capitalization. The containment procedures are rather disorganized as well; try to group similar information together rather than having it all sort of scattered and in need of clear flow/transition between topics.

Address these issues first and let me know when you have done so; I will then provide a full review of the draft.

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your crit. I adjusted most of it.
I stripped the blank-name of the MTF because they are just a side detail.
I would like to keep the reason for "Michael" to get in - accidents happen, at the unluckiest times.
You are right, I was trying to bypass research for an actual tracer (dont think such a specific one actually exists; traceable from orbit in low quanties AND safe for humans? uhhhh), so I just made one up now.

I will see to add more anomaly information in the coming days. Thanks again.

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Note, I am not the most well-read or experienced user. Reach out to members of the Butterfly Roster for more informed criticism.

Phrases in quotes are my suggestions.

Line By Line
hiya howdy howya doin

The hallway leading to SCP-XXXX has to be guarded by at least one security personnel at all times.

The hallway is to be guarded. Passive voice. Also, the "at least one" clause is unnecessary. How can a hallway be guarded by less than one guard?

Cleaning staff may flush if they hear noises coming from SCP-XXXX, but must record when they do so.

"Cleaning staff are to flush if they hear noises coming from SCP-XXXX, and must make record of doing so."

At no time should SCP-XXXX be used as originally intended.

Too vague. If we haven't read the article yet, we don't know what the original intent is.
"At no time should SCP-XXXX be used as a waste receptacle."

Side note: add line breaks between paragraphs. Necessary for readability.

The building housing SCP-XXXX has been bought by the Foundation and is used as [REDACTED]. To the outside it is advertised as telemarketing firm. Unauthorized entry should be responded to by calling the local police.

The ConProcs don't generally need detail about the Site cover stories unless it's related to the nature of the anomaly. Also, there are armed guards in this building. Involvement of local police is redundant. "Provisional Site-XXXX has been established in the building housing SCP-XXXX. Unauthorized entry is forbidden."

It consists of two adjacent restrooms, one for males and one for females.

"It consists of two adjacent restrooms with standard male/female designations."

Both areas have two sinks and four stalls

"Both areas possess"

The restrooms are working as normally expected.

"SCP-XXXX functions as expected for a public restroom."

as underground exploration and sub-surface scans showed.

"have shown"

Electricity however is connected as expected.

Commas after "electricity" and "however".

The planning company found that no plans existed where the water supply or sewer access was depicted for the building housing SCP-XXXX.

"Contractors found that water supply and sewer access were absent from all plans of the building."

A check of the canalization confirmed that no access to the building exists and the Foundation was informed.

"A check of the canalization confirmed the absence of water mains and sewer lines. The Foundation was subsequently notified."

The initially deployed MTF ███ secured SCP-XXXX under cover of the reconstruction project which was immediately canceled.

No reason to censor an MTF. "MTF-BLANK initially secured SCP-XXXX under cover of the renovation project. All construction plans were subsequently cancelled."

The employees of the offices in the building were detained and questioned. During the interviews medical and psychological examinations were conducted as well.

"Employees of the offices in the building were detained, questioned, and subjected to medical and psychological examination."

There was no indication of any influence on the persons working in the building.

This is simply untrue, given the information you provide in the next sentence.

Dr. Vitruv noted during the interviews that many employees had rather fond memories of the restrooms, finding relief being there, using the facilities or simply running the water.

"Dr. Vitruv noted that during the interviews, many employees recalled fond memories of the restrooms. Subjects reported feelings of calm or relief when using the facilities or simply running the water."

Sampling the tap water, it was discovered that it matches the composition and requirements of most of the tap water in the United States as shown in document XXXX-2.

"Sampling of the tap water revealed that it meets all composition requirements in the state of ██. It possesses no components that might aid in tracing its origin. For details on the composition of water obtained from SCP-XXXX, see Document-XXXX-2."

For the used water / waste see Post-Experiment report XXXX-4

"For compositional analysis of black- and grey-water obtained from SCP-XXXX, see Post-experiment Report XXXX-4."

Experiment XXXX-1: Audio Transcript

Add a note clarifying that the exploration is taking place via drone.

Frank:

Use Frank's full blacked-out name.

Note: Line breaks should be added throughout this log.

Note2: During this log there are multiple instances of ellipses ("…") that are spaced incorrectly. They should be placed directly after the word they follow with no space in-between.

As per experiment report XXXX-4-B and under strict safety measures four point one litres of [REDACTED] were inserted into the sewer section of SCP-XXXX using the first booth of the men's room. The liquid was flushed using a total of eighty litres of SCP-XXXX tap water. As [REDACTED] is a potent and safe tracer it was believed to enable us to identify the exit of SCP-XXXX. Unfortunately we did not manage to confirm any result.
About two months after the experiment a meteorological satellite under control of the ████ found traces of the used substance in the southern Atlantic. It is currently unknown if this finding correlates to SCP-XXXX.
I am awaiting clearance to repeat the experiment.
Dr. Vitruv

I have multiple issues with this note. Firstly, redacting the tracer liquid adds nothing to the article and makes the note significantly harder to read. Appears as if you simply did not want to research a traceable liquid. Similarly, there is no reason to redact the controller of the satellite. Lastly, there are multiple instances of missing commas. Dr. Vitruv should sign the note with a dash, like this:
"—Dr. Vitruv"

a man calling himself Michael (actual identity unknown, assumed to be a local homeless man)

"a local homeless man calling himself "Michael" (actual identity unconfirmed)"

The hallway guard was absent at that time due to a medical emergency.

This seems like gross incompetence on behalf of whoever is managing containment. Perhaps,

"The hallway guard was momentarily absent during shift turnover."

According to post-incident interrogation Michael had to urgently use the restroom, so he opened the (due to the emergency unlocked) front door and walked into SCP-XXXX.

"According to post-incident interrogation Michael urgently needed to use the restroom, and therefore entered SCP-XXXX through the main door, which was momentarily unlocked due to REASON"

Note: you're going to have to come up with a new reason for the door being unlocked. I can't think of one off the top of my head.

He described hearing a violent grown directly after he flushed - and experiencing a sharp pain in the lower abdomen before loosing consciousness.

"He described hearing a violent groan directly after flushing, and experienced a sharp lower-abdominal pain before losing consciousness."

bleeding from a head wound due to a broken door.

The meaning of this is unclear. How exactly did Michael hurt his head?

Overall thoughts
phew that took a while

While I overall enjoyed this skip, I don't believe it's quite ready for the mainlist in its current state. Specifically, the anomalous effect needs to be fleshed out. It's just… missing a little something.

Now, I very much enjoy how your article creates mystery, so going forward you have a tightrope to walk between showing us interesting and intriguing effects, and maintaining the simplicity of the premise. That's a difficult task, but I believe it can be done.

In conclusion I would say that perhaps 10% more information about the anomaly would add some much-needed intrigue, but 15% would be too much. Act on that as you see fit.

I wish you the best of luck and hope to see this on the mainlist sometime soon.

Have a great day!

item.title: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
A strange restroom that never had been connected to the public infrastructure. It has something strange, making people go there more often. Other than that rather harmless.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Brief: A restroom that has a connection to someplace other that the infrastructure surrounding it. It is somewhat behaving like an entity or part of one. Due to reactions with people it acts like some digestive tract.

Greenlight (2): http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13809212/seeking-greenlight:disconnected-restroom
Draft: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/galcedion
Word count: 1094 (current revision)

My first SCP-draft but I hope it meets the guidelines. So no specifics to check. For those who read - thanks in advance!
